clue.text: It should be better than 20/20 for management

blocks.note: something better than the ordinary is super
20/20 is the standard measure of perfect eyesight

explanation.surface: A boast that some quality ought to beat perfect eyesight, offered as a management philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as one idea: eyesight better than 20/20 would be SUPER VISION, which joins up as SUPERVISION.
explanation.definitionFit: Supervision is the overseeing and directing of staff or work, which is what management means here.

clue.text: Silk-screen an angel on the outside of semi

indicators.note: being on the outside of something means wrapping around it

blocks.note: a seraph is an angel of the highest order
in American usage a semi, or rig, is an articulated truck

explanation.surface: Printing an angel design onto the side of an articulated truck.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi here is not half of something but the American word for a big truck, also called a rig.
explanation.definitionFit: A serigraph is a print made by the silk-screen process, so the two name the same kind of artwork.

clue.text: Eastern agent going north, eating meat in spread

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
eating means taking something inside

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a rep, or representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: A spy from the East travelling north, eating meat at a spread of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a buffet in the surface, but it is a verb meaning to diffuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread throughout something, as a smell permeates a room.

clue.text: Polish-Estonian's foremost countryman

indicators.note: foremost picks out the leading letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: Asks for a Polish-Estonian man's leading compatriot.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P disguises polish the verb as Polish the nationality, a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A rube is US slang for an unsophisticated country dweller, a countryman in the rustic sense.

clue.text: Organizing NC, RI sit-in is essential

indicators.note: organizing means putting into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Activists say staging a sit-in across North Carolina and Rhode Island is vital.
explanation.walkthrough: NC and RI are the postal abbreviations for North Carolina and Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic means belonging to the basic nature of a thing, which is what essential means.

clue.text: Sailed at sea with aspirations

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone set out on a voyage full of hopes and ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' sits naturally beside sailed, hiding its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are the standards or goals one aims for, so they are aspirations.

clue.text: Organic hemoglobin has a role in the food chain

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the answer is held across the preceding words

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A biology statement that the blood pigment of living things plays a part in feeding relationships.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology a niche is the position and function a species occupies within its ecosystem, including its place in feeding chains.

clue.text: Television network is more evenhanded when avoiding false start

indicators.note: avoiding a start means the opening letter of the word is left off

explanation.surface: A claim that some TV channel is more impartial once it stops making false starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' is surface colour: the start is simply the first letter, F, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A network broadcasts, or airs, programmes, so it can whimsically be called an airer, one that puts shows on air.

clue.text: Barmen teach mixing in front room

indicators.note: mixing means stirring things together into a new order

explanation.surface: Bartenders give cocktail-making lessons in the front room.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixing fits the bartending scene, which is what hides it as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An antechamber is a small room leading into a larger one, an outer or front room.

clue.text: Smallish bra containing, say, a flower

indicators.note: containing tells us one piece holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a B cup is one of the smaller bra sizes
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A lingerie item, fairly small, that somehow holds a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The bra size is two pieces, a letter and a cup, and the second block slips between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wildflower of meadows.

clue.text: Show guy entering ineluctably

indicators.note: entering means going inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Some showman inevitably comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is a show put on before an audience.

clue.text: Idea: go to back, naked or dressed for a frat party

indicators.note: naked means stripped of outer layers, so the outer letters of the phrase are dropped
going to the back means reading the letters from the end toward the start

blocks.note: these words read from the end, with the first and last letters stripped off

explanation.surface: Pondering whether to go to the back of the room naked or in costume at a fraternity party.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse 'Idea go to' to get otogaedi, then strip one letter from each end. Toga parties are a staple of American college fraternity life.
explanation.definitionFit: Togaed means wearing a toga, the classic costume for a fraternity toga party.

clue.text: Elk riled wild bird

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An angry elk, and a wild bird somewhere in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riled' looks like it might be the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'wild' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The killdeer is a North American plover named for its shrill call.

clue.text: Social changes capturing attention — they can help you win an election

definitions.text: they can help you win an election

indicators.note: changes tells us the word before it is rearranged
capturing means the rearranged word holds another piece inside it

blocks.note: att. is a standard abbreviation for attention on letters and memos

explanation.surface: A political observation that shifts in society draw notice and help candidates win votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention' looks like plain surface, but its memo abbreviation is the piece placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a popular figure's coattails means being carried into office by their success, so coattails help win elections.

clue.text: Davenport plunges into topic that's arcane by definition

indicators.note: arcane means mysterious and obscure, so the word before it is scrambled out of recognition
plunging into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a davenport is a large sofa in American usage

explanation.surface: A writer dives into a subject so obscure it is defined as such.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arcane by definition' reads as one phrase, but arcane is the anagram signal and 'by definition' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for by that very fact, meaning something follows automatically, as by definition does.

clue.text: City in Czechoslovakia

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the next word, spanning some of its letters

blocks.note: letters five to eight of this word

explanation.surface: Asks for a city in the former Central European country of Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Prague or Bratislava, but the city is a Scandinavian capital lurking in the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Communication between ships and shore about excellent chart

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the others

blocks.note: in some American school grading E stands for excellent

explanation.surface: Messages passed between vessels and land concerning a superb navigational chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ships and shore' reads as one phrase, but shore belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling system using flags or arms, traditionally used for messages from ship to ship.

clue.text: Bloody sacrifice, as both came unglued

indicators.note: coming unglued means falling apart, so the letters break up and reassemble

explanation.surface: A gory offering in which two people lose their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came' does double duty: it is fodder and also part of the signal 'came unglued'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was an ancient Greek ritual slaughter of many cattle, hence a bloody sacrifice.

clue.text: Longing internalized by preacher

indicators.note: something internalized is held inside, so the answer sits within the next word

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A yearning that a minister has taken to heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it, so an ache can be a longing.

clue.text: Suburban voter shouted, "Punch her, Somerset!"

indicators.note: shouted means the words are spoken out, so we go by their sound

blocks.note: sock means punch, and Somerset Maugham was the English novelist

explanation.surface: A voter in the suburbs bellowing at someone called Somerset to hit a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset looks like the English county, but it is the novelist W. Somerset Maugham, addressed by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer mom is US political shorthand for a suburban mother, treated as a key swing-voter group.

clue.text: Athletic competitions, with energy, boosted prize

indicators.note: in a down clue, boosted means pushed upwards, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Track contests, run with extra vigour, raised the value of the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' looks like a noun for the trophy, but it is the verb meaning to value.
explanation.definitionFit: To prize something is to value it highly, which is to esteem it.

clue.text: Military policemen and chief of operations involved in fan's murders

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so these pieces go within the next word

blocks.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan

explanation.surface: Army police and an operations chief are mixed up in a fan's killing spree.
explanation.walkthrough: BUFF opens after BU to take in MPS and O. The 's stands for 'has': the fan has these pieces inside. Chief of means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump off is slang for to kill, so bumps off means murders.

clue.text: Bit of Morse code uploaded in French wine region

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter
in a down clue, uploaded means sent upwards, so the letters read in reverse

explanation.surface: A snippet of Morse code sent online from a wine-growing area of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse code' reads as one unit, but the clue takes a bit of Morse and adds the word code.
explanation.definitionFit: The Médoc is the area of Bordeaux, France, famous for its red wines.

clue.text: Throw cold water on, to block writer

blocks.note: to dam is to block a flow
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Discouraging someone so as to give them writer's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block writer' looks like writer's block, but block and writer are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing cold water on an idea discourages it, as does dampening enthusiasm; both are idioms for deflating.

clue.text: Fill belly with victual, ultimately!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is taken
with here means carrying something inside

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to stuff their stomach with provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: To glut is to fill to excess, to stuff full.

clue.text: Deranged prince led censor

indicators.note: deranged means thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mad royal ruler who led the censorship of his realm.
explanation.definitionFit: To red-pencil is to cut or censor text, from the editor's habit of marking deletions in red.

clue.text: Gas found in Discworld?

blocks.note: a zone is a sphere or realm, a world of its own
surface padding: the whole word is Pratchett's fantasy setting, which the setter splits into the two pieces above

explanation.surface: Wondering which gas you would find in Terry Pratchett's fantasy Discworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Discworld is Pratchett's flat, disc-shaped fantasy world; the question mark flags that it is to be split into disc and world.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a pungent gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Easy at first: chant "om" for food

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: Meditation advice: take it easy at the start, chanting om in exchange for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy at first' looks like it should give the letter E, but Easy is the definition and 'at first' belongs to chant.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfortable describes a relaxed, untroubled state, so it can mean easy, as in an easy chair.
